meta.note: Single source of truth. Every value traces to a guide section or a logged decision. CSS, the skill and the Office theme are generated FROM this file — never hand-edited. If a value is needed that the guide does not define, that is a gap: log it in docs/gaps.md, do not invent a token. v1.5.1 (14 Oct 2026) amends the voice and editorial sections only; no value in this file changed. v1.5 (5 Oct 2026) adds type.voices, type.steps, the 26 named type roles and the four line weights, decided with Carly Heath across review rounds one to seven, 4–5 October 2026.
supersedes: Nightlife Culture Style Guide v1.4.2 DRAFT (not adopted)

blue.role: Primary ground. Covers, dividers, statements, links.

ink.role: Night ground. Full-bleed surfaces and strips where accents need to glow.

white.role: Reading ground — reports and print; panels on chalk.

accents.comment: Surface palette only. COL-06 (Fixed): never encode data in these.

pink.role: Hot counter-signal, accent bars, left rules
pink.ratioNote: ink text on pink — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

teal.role: Cool highlight, section headers on dark
teal.ratioNote: ink text on teal — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

violet.ratioNote: ink text on violet — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

butter.ratioNote: ink text on butter — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

coral.ratioNote: ink text on coral — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

chartRamp.comment: Data only. Four series maximum (DAT-04, Fixed). Direct labelling is the compliance mechanism (COL-12, Fixed) — decide labelling before colour (COL-11).
chartRamp.warning: Book ch04 measured: under protanopia series 1 and 2 render at 1.10:1 and the lightness order inverts. Do not claim this ramp survives all CVD.

neutralsRemoved.note: REMOVED 16 Aug 2026. #D8D8D8 #A6A6A6 #6E6E6E #4A4A4A were read out of v1.4 §12 where they render the GREYSCALE DEMONSTRATION of the chart ramp — the desaturated strip proving lightness climbs monotonically. They are a rendering artefact, not tokens. Promoting them into the palette invented four greys nobody approved.

colour.greysPolicy: There are no greys. Ink #0D0D0D, charcoal #2D2D2D, chalk #F3F3F3 and white #FFFFFF cover every neutral need. Anything between them is an invention.

ink.role: Primary text colour on chalk and white.
ink.usedAs: text; also the night ground (see grounds.ink)

charcoal.role: Secondary copy, captions, slide titles on light grounds.
charcoal.note: Moved out of grounds 16 Aug 2026. It was listed as a ground carrying textOn 'white' and the ratio 12.41 — which is charcoal TEXT on CHALK, not white text on charcoal. Right number, wrong frame. Nothing in the system uses charcoal as a ground.

theLaw.statement: Every accent takes ink text. Every ground takes the text colour its own token declares — white on blue and ink, ink on chalk and white.
theLaw.supersedes: 'Every ground is a white-text surface.' That is false for two of the four grounds: white text on chalk is 1.1096:1 and white on white is 1.0000:1. The per-ground data in this file was always correct; the memorable sentence was not, which is worse, because the sentence is what gets remembered.
theLaw.readThisNotThat: Read the ground off tokens.json. Never off a remembered sentence.

faces.note: Inter 500 and 600 are embedded for the slide layer only. The document layer uses Inter 400, Inter 700 for emphasis and the first column of a table, and Inter 400 Italic for a short run inside a paragraph.

roles.note: The 26 named type styles (rounds four to seven, 4–5 Oct 2026). The name is the class and the Word style is built from the same row. 'element' is the HTML element the style sits on where that is fixed; a heading style sits only on its own heading element and h5 and h6 are barred (NC-CON-04).

heading-1.note: Break to two lines rather than shrinking.

contents-title.use: A title in a contents list

number.use: Section and chapter numbers on an ink box; page numbers

heading-4.use: The lowest heading, with its blue bar. The floor: there is no H5 or H6

takeaway.use: One or two sentences to remember, in the running text with a pink rule

key-statement.use: The question or point a chapter turns on, in its top-rule panel

button.use: The one thing to press. Blue, fully rounded

text-action.use: A minor action beside a button, underlined

quotation.use: A quotation that runs on, in the running text with a pink rule

table-first-column.use: The first column of a table, which names each row. Bold

file-reference.use: A file name or literal string, on a white hairline chip. Never monospace

small.use: Notes under tables and charts, source lines, small print, hints

chip.use: Status, on a fill. The word carries the meaning, never the colour alone

evidence-mark.use: A bracketed mark inside a sentence

attribution.use: Who said it, under a quotation

pattern.source: Measured from Artists Make Great Places v2.0 (Carly Heath, September 2026) — the first live deck adopted as reference. pt on a 13.33in (960pt) slide; the stylesheet converts pt to cqw as pt / 9.6.

table.status: PROPOSAL — the live deck set its budget table at 9.4pt; 12pt is the v1.4 document body minimum. A table on a slide is for a deck that is sent and read, not projected (NC-PRS-03). If it does not fit at 12pt, it is two slides.

lineHeight.note: measured on the reference deck: 18pt body on 22pt leading

scale.source: Nightlife Culture Style Guide v1.5: the six steps in type.steps. Kept here in the form the Office adapters read. h4, small and label added 5 Oct 2026; note is the old name for small.

note.from: v1.4 footnotes and caveats — 10pt minimum, 10.5-11pt preferred

h4.from: round two: H4 is body size, Archivo Bold, with a blue bar above

small.from: round two: two small roles, small at 14px

label.from: round two: the label voice at 12px, 10pt in print. The one style under the 13px note floor, and a phrase, never a sentence

base.source: v1.4 Readable size rules — document body 12pt minimum AND preferred. 12pt = 16px.

rhythm.source: ch03 — 'section headings carry 3x the space above them that they carry below, so they attach to what follows rather than floating between blocks.'

display.source: ch03 — display and covers are the decorative tier, 'no meaning carried, no accessibility cost provided a text equivalent exists. This is where a house voice lives and it should be used hard.' Free by the Book's own rule, so this needs no decision — but it is named as decorative, not as a step.

label.status: DECIDED 5 Oct 2026 — one number: 12px on screen, 10pt in print, the label voice only
label.why: Round two, confirmed round three. v1.4 gave slide labels only. In a document the label is a phrase in capitals above or beside a thing, and at 12px it stays under the heading it labels. It is the only style under the 13px note floor (NC-TYP-06) and under the 16pt caps floor besides the 14px titles (NC-TYP-04).

capsFloor.exceptions: The fixed small styles only: contents-title and table-title at 14px, and the label voice and number at 12px (NC-TYP-04, v1.5).

was.note: Resolves the v1.4 §08 internal conflict (labels stated at 14pt minimum, H3 note states caps stop working below 16pt) in favour of 16. Adaptable.

voices.note: The primary rule for type (decided 5 Oct 2026, round four). Every text style is one voice at one step. A component may place text, colour it and put a line beside it. It never sets a typeface, a size, a weight or capitals of its own. The display voice is the one exception to the six steps: it is sized to the cover.

display.use: Covers and mastheads only. Sized to the cover, never a step.

capitals.use: Headings one and two, titles in contents and tables, numbers.
capitals.note: Tracking compensates for optical tightening as caps shrink; heading-1 at 32px takes 0.01em.

sentence.use: Headings three and four, the takeaway, the key statement, the button.

text.use: Running text and everything that reads like it. Bold (700) for emphasis and the first column of a table. Italic for a short run inside a paragraph.

label.use: A phrase, never a sentence: labels, table header rows, chips, evidence marks, attributions, the running foot.

steps.note: Six sizes and no others (round four). Screen px against a 16px base, print pt against a 12pt body. The caps floor for headings is 16pt; below it, capitals appear only in the fixed small styles named in the roles.

headings.rule: A heading style sits only on its own element: nc-heading-1 on h1 through nc-heading-4 on h4. A collapsible heading keeps the style of its level (NC-CON-04, NC-DOC-10).

slide.status: DECIDED 16 Aug 2026 — the measured geometry, snapped to a unit.
slide.why: The written 6% / 7.5% flat was a real decision flattened to a constant. What the decks actually do is vary the top margin by what leads the slide, and that variation is the mechanism that guides the reader: a kicker is small and quiet so it can sit high, because it is not the message; a statement needs air above it to land. Give the title the kicker's margin and the slide top-loads — the composition loses the breath that makes the rest of the system work. So the three steps stay, snapped to one unit so every value is a multiple (ch02, Fixed).
slide.footerNote: Reserved on EVERY slide, covers and closers included. The band is not there because a number is printed in it — it is there because in a physical room the bottom of the screen is the hardest place to read: heads sit in the sightline. That reason does not change when the number does, so it is one grid, not two (ch12, readability from the back of the room).
slide.symmetry: The footer band and the largest top step are both ten units, so a slide led by a full-bleed element sits in a centred band. That is a consequence of the unit, not a separate rule.

supersedes.note: Measured 3.87 / 6.67 / 13.33 land on 3 / 5 / 10 units within 0.13 of a percentage point. The measured 6.4% footer is rejected: it is what the old decks did, not what the room needs.

pattern.source: Measured from Artists Make Great Places v2.0 (Carly Heath, September 2026) — the first live deck adopted as reference. pt on a 13.33in (960pt) slide; the stylesheet converts pt to cqw as pt / 9.6.
pattern.bottomNote: Content in the live deck runs to about 92% of slide height; the reserved 13.333% footer band holds only a slide number where there is one. 6 units.
pattern.closingBandNote: The full-width closing band measured 17.7–18.9% of height; snapped to 13 units.
pattern.ruleWeightNote: Column and callout rules measured 4pt — the separator breaker weight (0.42% of width).
pattern.sideBlockNote: The accent third on the live deck bleeds off the right edge from 71.3% of width.

separator.colour: blue on light, teal on dark

accentBar.use: Above a pull quote only. The one decorative use.

scale.note: One base unit, .25em, everything a multiple. Short (9 steps) and non-linear — increments widen as values grow, because perceived difference is proportional. em so it scales with context, like every component. ch02, Fixed.

slideScale.note: Measured from the hand-built decks and recorded in joy.css, where it was defined and never used. Percentages of slide width.

direction.position: Minimalist. Bright colours as set out. Plenty of breathing space to let the message carry.
direction.principle: The joy comes from what we are up to, not from ornament. The decision layer keeps the message in check.

lines.note: Four weights of line and no others (round six and seven, 5 Oct 2026). A line that goes with text is a rule. A line on a filled box is a callout line. Each weight is double the one before and all four are in Word's own border menu. Fixed sizes, not em: the same line was thicker on larger text before.

hair.use: Table rows, contents rows, outlines, the foot of a page. Never carries meaning (NC-CON-02).

table.use: Under a table's header row. Half the rule, in proportion to the 12px headings it sits under.

rule.use: A line that goes with text: section title, H4 bar, breaker, rail marker, quotation, comparability flag.

callout.use: A line on a filled box, at the top or the left: key statement, callout, recommendation, Claude note, statistic, chart card, accent table.

nightTime.rule: Night time is two words, never hyphenated: night time economy, Night Time Advisor.

language.culturalValue: cultural value and cultural contribution are not interchangeable; use the one you mean
